name: xc-typed-errors-implement
description: How to build the typed-error guarantee on the stack that actually runs: why there is no incumbent to migrate from, what the first implementation is when the enforcement machinery available today is a check that sits outside the enforcement path, the second implementation that moves the check from build time over the tree to run time over live responses, the three-step migration that can each ship alone, where the budget, policy, identity, correlation and idempotency guarantees land as declared members of a failure body, and the definition of done that fails when a retry heuristic starts reading words again. Load it when converting a real failure site to the typed object, when wiring the string-match gate or the per-boundary untyped counter, when deciding which of the two checks a green run has actually exercised, when a refusal has to carry a policy rule or a budget figure, or when an audit reports zero and you need to know whether anything failed at all.

purpose.text: Turn the guarantee stated in xc-typed-errors into a build on what runs here: nothing types failures today and the only verification machinery on hand runs outside the path it checks, so this facet is an adoption over call sites plus a second implementation that proves the check is not tuned to the moment it happens to run.

shapes.name: TypedErrorsConformanceReport (proposed): the machine-readable output the definition of done asserts on, one object per implementation run; it extends the TypedErrorAudit shape xc-typed-errors owns with the fields that identify which implementation produced it

implementation.description: Which of the two produced this report. A label only; no assertion branches on it.

selected_by.description: A code edit between the two runs is the finding, not the setup.

checks_at.description: The axis the pair differs on: the whole tree before anything runs, or live responses as they leave a boundary.

audit.description: The report shape xc-typed-errors defines: parser_path, string_match_sites, failures_checked, untyped, unregistered_types, per_entry.

observed_population.description: What this implementation could actually see. A build-time run sees code paths that never execute; a run-time run sees only what did.

evidence_record_ref.description: The evidence record this run was written into: script digest, commit, tree hash under test, dirty flag, and the claimed-or-measured label.

invariants.text: xc-typed-errors owns the guarantee, its scope over every failure-producing site, the one shared registry behind every driving adapter, and the audit report shape (F-b4-07). Nothing here restates it. This facet owns three things only: when the check executes, how the two implementations are selected, and how a run is recorded.

There is no incumbent to migrate from. The recorded adapter for this capability is absent, so the migration is over call sites rather than over an implementation, and no measured behaviour is inherited from anything running today.

The failure this build has to avoid is already on file in the same inventory that records typed errors as missing: conformance checks exist; not wired into the enforcement path. xc-typed-errors states that a check outside the enforcement path is not this guarantee; the consequence for the build is that a string-match audit which runs and reports without blocking reproduces that arrangement exactly, under a new name.
invariants.quote: Conformance checks exist; not wired into the enforcement path

invariants.text: The two implementations differ in when the check executes and therefore in what it can see, not in which product supplies it. build-adapter-pair owns the rule and the axis test (F-b1-04); what this facet adds is that swappability is a tested property, not an intention has a specific meaning here, namely that a build-time tree scan and a run-time response interceptor must report the same counts over the same conversion state.
invariants.quote: Swappability is a tested property, not an intention.

invariants.text: Proposed: neither implementation may invent a type it was not given. An interceptor that guesses a type from the words in a body is the string matching this guarantee bans, relocated into the enforcement layer, where it is harder to see and impossible for the tree scan to find.

Every audit run is written into an evidence record before its numbers are read, and a run from a dirty tree is never labelled measured. build-evidence-record owns the record's fields and agentic-stack owns the labelling rule; the consequence here is that untyped and string_match_sites are exactly the kind of number that gets repeated later, and an unlabelled zero becomes a measurement the moment someone quotes it.
invariants.quote: Each record names the script SHA-256, git commit, tree hash under test, and whether the tree was dirty

not_exposed.text: Proposed: which implementation is enforcing is invisible to every failure-producing site and to every caller. A producer that could tell them apart would learn to satisfy the cheaper one, and the swap would stop being free.

Proposed: no configuration key, environment flag or fast-path exemption disables the audit or the counters for a deployment. xc-typed-errors states why a caller cannot decline the guarantee (F-b1-08); the consequence for the build is that the off switch must not exist in the configuration surface either, or a zero becomes a statement about how one environment was set up.

Proposed: the untyped payload an adapter-unavailable problem carries in detail is not a branch key and is scrubbed of hostnames, credentials and adapter identities before it is carried. It exists so a human can find the site that failed to type, not so a caller can resume parsing prose from a new place.

instructions.action: Start by narrowing the return type, not by converting sites: make the typed object the only failure return declared on the dispatch seam's result shape, before a single failure site is rewritten.
instructions.why: The seam is where the contract has to say what a failure returns, and narrowing the type first turns every unconverted site into a compile-or-validation error that names itself, instead of a search someone has to remember to run.
instructions.quote: It must specify: the request shape, the result shape, cancellation semantics, timeout and budget enforcement, partial-result handling, and what a failure returns.

instructions.action: Migrate in three steps that can each ship alone: first add the object and the shared registry and convert the seam; second run the tree audit and the per-boundary untyped counters read-only and record the counts as claimed; third turn both into gates. Do not merge steps two and three.
instructions.why: Proposed. A gate switched on over a population nobody has counted turns a migration into an outage on its first run, and the read-only pass is also the only way to learn which failure sites exist rather than which ones were remembered.

instructions.action: Convert boundaries in the order of the enforcement table in xc-typed-errors' references: the policy refusal, the budget termination and the envelope validation failure first, and assert their type agreement across the three ways in before converting anything else.
instructions.why: Proposed. Those three are the refusals the fold-in requires to carry the same machine-readable type whichever way the caller entered, so they are the ones whose disagreement would be designed in if they were converted last, each by whoever owned that path.

instructions.action: Add the second implementation as an interceptor in each boundary's response path, counting and refusing untyped bodies as they leave, and change no failure site to get it.
instructions.why: This is composability doing the work the target asks of it: enhancing particular aspects of any element without touching the rest. Enforcement moves to run time, no producer is edited, and the check now runs where a compiled dependency's untyped failure is visible, which the tree scan can never read.
instructions.quote: Composability allows enhancing particular aspects of any element without touching the rest.

instructions.action: Wire the cross-cutting guarantees onto the failure body as declared extension members, adding them to the problem shape rather than to a logging helper: the correlation identifiers, the actor and its delegation chain, the spend at the moment a budget terminated a unit, the policy rule identifier on a refusal, and the idempotency key the attempt was made under.
instructions.why: Proposed. Every action already names an actor including delegated agent actors, and the failure body is often the only artifact that crosses the boundary and survives the process, so a guarantee that lives only in a log line is absent from the one record the caller actually holds.

instructions.action: Convert the consumers before the producers where you have a choice: rewrite each retry loop and each error-handling branch to key on the type member first, then narrow the producer that feeds it.
instructions.why: Proposed. A producer converted under a consumer that still matches on words changes behaviour silently, because the words moved and the match stopped firing; a consumer converted first fails loudly on the type it has not been given yet.

instructions.action: Write every audit run into an evidence record before reading its numbers: the script digest, the commit, the tree hash under test, whether the tree was dirty, and the claimed-or-measured label. Record the observed population alongside each count.
instructions.why: build-evidence-record owns the record's fields and agentic-stack owns the labelling rule (F-part-c-08); what this step adds is the population, because a build-time run and a run-time run over the same tree legitimately see different denominators, and two zeros with no denominators cannot be compared.

instructions.action: Run the identical audit against both implementations with the choice made in configuration only, and treat any code edit needed between the two runs as the finding rather than as setup.
instructions.why: build-adapter-pair states the discipline and the axis test; the failure mode specific to this guarantee is a check written as a grep invocation, which cannot run at all against an interceptor that has no source tree to read, so the report shape rather than the command has to be what the assertions are written against.
instructions.quote: chosen to prove the interface is not shaped around its current implementation

instructions.action: Proposed: open references/migration-and-wiring.md for the per-implementation conformance subset, the cross-cutting wiring table, and the boundary-by-boundary conversion checklist. This skill body is enough to plan and judge the build without it.
instructions.why: Proposed, progressive disclosure. The subset and the checklist change every time a boundary or an implementation is added, and material on that cadence does not belong in the body a reviewer reads once.

best_practices.text: Do not read the first green run as a typed system. agentic-stack, build-definition-of-done and build-evidence-record all build on the finding that a gate can be structurally green because the work contained nothing the tools apply to, and those establish well-formedness, not correctness; the version of it here is an audit over a tree where nothing has been converted, which reports zero string matches and zero untyped failures, both true and both meaningless.

Verify that the interceptor actually saw the response rather than that it was configured to. agentic-stack states the finding that configuration written in the documented place can be silently overridden and build-evidence-record and build-adapter-pair both build on it (F-a7-04); the version here is an interceptor registered in the right file and bypassed by one boundary that writes its response directly, which is invisible unless the report counts what it observed.

Proposed: count non-conformant bodies in the interceptor and never drop them. A stage that silently discards what it cannot verify produces a clean report from a broken system, which is the same shape of green that this platform has already measured once.

Proposed: when the two implementations disagree, believe the one that saw more. A build-time scan finding a string-matching site the interceptor never reported means that path did not execute, not that the site is acceptable; an interceptor counting an untyped body the scan never flagged means the failure came from beneath the source tree, which is why the pair exists.

adapters.maps_to: Nothing types failures today: the recorded adapter for this capability is absent, so the first implementation of this guarantee is a build-time audit over the source tree, run as one more automated verification stage beside the deployment phases that already exist, plus the in-process typing layer it checks. Its execution model is a whole-tree static scan that runs before anything executes and needs no traffic and no running system.
adapters.cannot: Cannot see a string match inside a compiled or vendored dependency, inside a prompt written at run time, or in a language its pattern does not cover; and cannot see an untyped failure at all, because it reads code rather than responses. It also cannot block anything by itself, which is precisely the arrangement PASS.md A6 already records against this platform, so it must be wired into the path rather than reported beside it.
adapters.swap_procedure: Select the implementation by configuration only, run the same assertions against the report shape rather than against the command, and require the merged report to show two implementations and selected_by configuration. xc-typed-errors owns the guarantee and cap-errors owns the failure object; what this row adds is that the audit's assertions are written against TypedErrorsConformanceReport so a scan and an interceptor can both satisfy them.
adapters.quote: Conformance checks exist; not wired into the enforcement path

adapters.maps_to: Proposed implementation, and a proposed entity id: no swap-candidate entity exists for this capability because, as cap-errors and xc-typed-errors both state, the recorded swap-candidate column is the instruction to adopt the RFC directly. It is an interceptor sitting in each boundary's response path at run time, which validates every outgoing failure body against the problem shape, increments that boundary's untyped counter when it does not conform, and refuses to pass the body on.
adapters.cannot: Cannot see a code path that did not execute, so a dormant string-matching retry heuristic is invisible to it until the day it fires; cannot read source at all; and must never infer a type from the words in a body it was handed, which would move the banned string matching into the enforcement layer. It needs a process on the response path where the first implementation needs none. The axis is when the check runs and what it can therefore see - the whole tree before execution against live responses during it - which is a different execution model rather than a different product of the same shape, and it is the axis that matters because each of the two is blind to exactly what the other sees.
adapters.swap_procedure: Select by configuration only, with no code edit between runs, and require both reports to validate against TypedErrorsConformanceReport and to carry distinct checks_at values with identical audit assertions. build-adapter-pair owns the rule that the second exists to prove the first is not load-bearing (F-b1-04); what this row adds is the observed_population the run-time implementation must publish, without which its zero cannot be compared with the scan's.

definition_of_done.criterion: docs/decomposition.md section 3.4 row X6, made precise and run over the pair above: `python3 tools/conformance/typed_errors_audit.py --implementation tree-scan --entry human --entry agent --entry event --report out/x6-a.json` then the same command with `--implementation response-interceptor --report out/x6-b.json` (proposed tool), the implementation chosen by configuration with no code edit between runs. Each run performs row X6's check - zero occurrences of failure information extracted by string matching anywhere outside the problem-details parser, `grep -rn -E 'match.*(error|failed|timeout)' src/ --include='*.py'` excluding `src/problem/` for the scan, the equivalent count over intercepted bodies for the interceptor - and raises one shared refusal under each of the three ways in. Both reports must validate against the TypedErrorsConformanceReport shape above and assert `string_match_sites == 0`, `untyped == 0`, `unregistered_types == 0`, `failures_checked > 0` per entry, `observed_population > 0`, and one distinct `shared_refusal_type`. Across runs it asserts two implementations, `selected_by == "configuration"`, and two distinct `checks_at` values.
definition_of_done.expected: both runs exit 0; each report shows `string_match_sites == 0`, `untyped == 0`, `unregistered_types == 0`, `observed_population > 0`, `failures_checked > 0` for each of the three entries and one distinct `shared_refusal_type`; the merged report shows two implementations, `selected_by == "configuration"`, `checks_at` values `build_time` and `run_time`, and both reports carry an `evidence_record_ref`.
definition_of_done.breakage: Add a retry heuristic that matches on the substring "rate limit" in a response body, in a module outside `src/problem/`, and make that module execute on one of the three entry paths. Leave both implementations, the fixtures and the command untouched.
definition_of_done.expected_failure: both runs exit 1 with `string_match_sites == 1`, the tree scan naming the file and line and the interceptor naming the boundary whose retry decision changed without a type; `untyped` stays 0 in both, which is what locates the defect in a consumer rather than in a producer. A run where only the tree scan fails means the heuristic never executed and the fixture does not exercise that path; a run where only the interceptor fails means the scan's pattern does not cover that module's language, and either asymmetry is the finding rather than a pass. Claimed: typed errors are absent, no failure site returns the object, neither implementation exists, `src/` and the audit tool are not written, so neither run has been performed here and the check starts red by construction.
definition_of_done.quote: plus the deliberate breakage that proves the check can fail

open_questions.question: When both implementations are deployed, which one enforces: the build-time scan, the run-time interceptor, or both?
open_questions.evidence: Run both read-only for one week over the same traffic and the same tree, and compare what each saw. If the interceptor counts untyped bodies the scan never flagged, enforcement belongs where the wider view is; if the counts agree, the cheaper one wins and the other stays a reporter.
open_questions.default: Both enforce, on different failures: the scan blocks a merge that introduces a string-matching site, the interceptor blocks an untyped body from leaving. Neither is allowed to invent a type. build-adapter-pair owns the two-adapter rule this question sits inside (F-b1-04); what is open is only which of the two enforces. Reversible by demoting one to reporting, which costs one configuration change and no producer change.
open_questions.quote: Every interface ships with at least two adapters

open_questions.question: Can this definition of done be run at all before any failure site is converted, given `failures_checked > 0` and `observed_population > 0` cannot be satisfied by a system that returns no typed failures?
open_questions.evidence: Whether any code path returns a problem object yet. The recorded state is that typed errors are absent, so today the answer is no for the typed half and yes for the string-match half.
open_questions.default: Run it and let it stay red, labelled claimed, rather than dropping the assertions that cannot yet pass. xc-typed-errors states that the starting state is red and correct (F-a6-06); dropping the population assertion is how a guarantee turns into a claim about the half that was easy.
open_questions.quote: A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion

open_questions.question: Does the interceptor sit inside each boundary's own process or in a separate process on the response path, given that the first arrangement shares the failure mode it is meant to catch and the second cannot see an in-process call that never becomes a response?
open_questions.evidence: Count, over the boundaries that exist, how many return a failure without producing a response another process could observe. If that count is large, an out-of-process interceptor is enforcing over a minority of the failures.
open_questions.default: In-process per boundary, because xc-typed-errors binds the guarantee to every failure-producing site rather than to every response (F-b4-07), and the axis the pair is chosen on is already build time against run time rather than in-process against out-of-process. Reversible by moving the same validator behind a proxy at the cost of the failures it would stop seeing.

open_questions.question: The second implementation has no swap-candidate entity in the knowledge base: E-swap-candidate-runtime-boundary-interceptor is an id minted in the adapters table here because the schema requires one and the recorded swap-candidate column for Errors is an instruction rather than a candidate list. Should it become a real entity, and what does the row cite until it is?
open_questions.evidence: 1-3-1 applied on 2026-09-03 (ceremony 9, finding C9-001), the protocol the wave-4c siblings used for the same gap. Options: (a) add the id to the knowledge base, which needs a rebuild and would invalidate the provenance heads of every skill already written; (b) collapse both rows onto E-adapter-errors-absent, the only entity this capability has, which would leave the two implementations indistinguishable in the very table the swap run reads; (c) keep the minted id, say in the row itself that both the implementation and the id are proposed, and record the gap here so a reader can tell it from a knowledge-base-backed id without grepping. Recommendation followed: (c), which is also what cap-errors-implement records for the same capability row. xc-typed-errors owns the reading of F-b3-13 that this guarantee builds on; what this row adds is which id the second implementation is recorded against until the entity exists. The question closes when a ceremony rebuilds the knowledge base and the entity exists.
open_questions.default: Keep the proposed id and the row's claimed status; do not list it under entities, where an invented id would silently satisfy the validator's unknown-id check; rely instead on the adapter-entity resolution warning ceremony 9 added to tools/validate_skills.py to keep it visible to every later reader.
